caseTitle: Arun Bhatiya v. HDFC Bank & Ors.
summary: Held that banking services rendered by commercial scheduled banks fall within the statutory definition of 'service' under Section 2(42) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and consumer commissions possess concurrent jurisdiction alongside DRT and SARFAESI proceedings.
keyPropositions: Consumer Protection Act 2019 Section 2(42) wide ambit of service explicitly encompasses banking facilities
Concurrent jurisdiction of consumer fora operates alongside SARFAESI and RDDBFI tribunals
Summary adjudication of banking deficiency without remitting consumer to civil court

iracBrief.facts: The appellant, Arun Bhatiya, held a savings account with HDFC Bank. Unauthorized debits were made from his account. When he approached the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, the bank argued that proceedings under the SARFAESI Act or RDDBFI Act barred the jurisdiction of consumer commissions.
issuesFramed: Whether banking services rendered to an individual constitute 'service' under Section 2(42) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
Whether the existence of remedies under specialized debt recovery statutes ousts the jurisdiction of Consumer Fora?
provisionsCited: Section 18, Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993
iracBrief.ratioDecidendi: The Supreme Court held that the definition of 'service' under Section 2(42) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 is inclusive and explicitly encompasses banking. The remedy under the Consumer Protection Act is an additional remedy, not in derogation of any other law, unless there is a clear and direct statutory exclusion.
iracBrief.finalOrderHeld: Appeal allowed. The order of the National Commission dismissing the consumer complaint was set aside, and the complaint was remitted for adjudication on merits.

## IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
### CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
**CIVIL APPEAL NO. 5208 OF 2022**

**ARUN BHATIYA ...APPELLANT(S)**

**VERSUS**

**HDFC BANK & ORS. ...RESPONDENT(S)**

### JUDGMENT
**Dr. Dhananjaya Y. Chandrachud, J.**

1. This appeal arises from a judgment dated 8 August 2022 of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission dismissing the consumer complaint filed by the appellant on the ground that banking disputes involving loan accounts must be relegated to civil court or specialized tribunals.

2. The primary question before this Court is whether the consumer forum possesses jurisdiction to adjudicate allegations of deficiency in banking services.

pages.pageMarkdown:
### ANALYSIS & RATIO DECIDENDI

14. Section 2(42) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 defines 'service' in expansive terms:

> 'service' means service of any description which is made available to potential users and includes, but is not limited to, the provision of facilities in connection with banking, financing, insurance, transport, processing, supply of electrical or other energy, telecom, boarding or lodging...

15. The legislative intent to retain banking within the consumer fold is unequivocal. The remedies under the Act are compensatory in nature and operate alongside special remedies under the SARFAESI Act.

16. Consequently, we hold that the consumer commission fell into patent error in declining to exercise jurisdiction.

caseTitle: Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Haryana & Anr.
summary: Held that General Power of Attorney (GPA), Agreement to Sell, and Will transactions (SA/GPA/WILL transfers) do not confer title and cannot substitute a registered deed of conveyance under Section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act.

caseTitle: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
summary: Unanimously affirmed the right to privacy as a fundamental right intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and Part III of the Constitution of India, establishing the proportionality test for state incursions.

iracBrief.finalOrderHeld: Reference answered in the affirmative; M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) overruled to the extent they held privacy was not a fundamental right.

An invasion of life or personal liberty must meet the three-fold requirement: (i) Legality, which postulates the existence of law; (ii) Need, defined in terms of a legitimate state aim; and (iii) Proportionality, which ensures a rational nexus between the objects and the means adopted to achieve them.
